title: Sorting: bubble and selection

youtube.title: C++ Sorting: Bubble Sort and Selection Sort | C++ Programming EP 40
youtube.description: In this episode you will trace a bubble sort, write a selection sort and count the compares and swaps, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Sorting: bubble and selection · 0:49 Bubble sort · 1:29 Bubble sort on five bars · 1:59 Second program · 2:59 Recap · 3:29 Bug of the Day · 4:17 Challenge · 4:37 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "SORT THE BARS" in tomato on butter; Xecxec next to five bars of different heights being swapped; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to five bars of different heights being swapped

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we sort. You will watch bars move, and then you will write the code that moves them.

scenes.onScreen: "Sorting: bubble and selection": numbered lines (1. Bubble sort swaps neighbours; 2. Selection sort picks the smallest; 3. Both use nested loops) and an analogy card: students lining up by height: neighbours swap places until the line is right
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Sorting puts items in order. Bubble sort compares two neighbours, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. After each pass, the biggest item has moved to the end. Selection sort finds the smallest item, and puts it first. Think of students who line up by height. Neighbours swap places until the line is right.

analogy.title: Sorting: bubble and selection
analogy.body: Students lining up by height: neighbours swap places until the line is right

scenes.onScreen: bubble.cpp: bubble sort with two loops and a swap
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 7] Each pass moves the biggest unsorted item to its place at the end. [HL 8] The inner loop visits each neighbour pair. The range gets shorter after each pass. [HL 9] If the left item is bigger, [HL 10] we swap the two items with a helper box. [HL 16] When all passes end, the array reads one, three, four, five, eight.

scenes.onScreen: bars compare, swap and turn mint as they reach their place
scenes.animation: Bars compare in butter, swap in tomato and slide past each other, sorted bars turn mint; pass, compare and swap counters tick
scenes.narration: Watch the bars. Two neighbours are compared. If the left one is taller, they swap. After the first pass, the tallest bar sits on the right. After each pass, one more bar turns mint. At the end, all bars are in order.

scenes.onScreen: selection.cpp: selection sort picks the smallest item each time
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 8] M holds the index of the smallest item that we know so far. [HL 9] The inner loop looks at all the items to the right. [HL 10] A smaller item becomes the new m. [HL 14] After the inner loop, we swap the smallest item into position i. Selection sort makes at most one swap for each pass.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as selection dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints one, three, four, five, eight.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. Bubble sort swaps neighbours that are out of order. Two. Selection sort swaps the smallest item to the front. Three. Both use nested loops. Four. Count the compares and swaps to compare the methods. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: Bubble sort swaps neighbours that are out of order.
Selection sort swaps the smallest item to the front.
Count the compares and swaps to compare the methods.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A swap that loses a value
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The array is three, one, two. The sorted output has repeated numbers. The swap has no helper box. The first line overwrites a j. The second line copies the same value back. Both boxes now hold one. Save the old value in a helper box first.

scenes.onScreen: Bubble sort is a patient algorithm. It takes many passes, and it never complains.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Bubble sort is a patient algorithm. It takes many passes, and it never complains.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Add a counter to bubble sort. Print how many swaps it made for the array five, three, eight, one, four. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: We end module four here. Next time: memory and addresses, the start of pointers. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

1 1 2
bug.why: The first line overwrites a at j. The second line then copies the new value back, so both boxes hold the same number. A helper box keeps the old value.

pun: "Bubble sort is a patient algorithm. It takes many passes, and it never complains."
challenge: Add a counter to bubble sort. Print how many swaps it made for the array five, three, eight, one, four.
challengeAnswer: Add one to a counter inside the if, next to the swap. For this array, the counter ends at six.
